title: Uber Ride Sharing: Complete Architecture
description: Design Uber-scale ride matching, real-time location tracking, surge pricing, and driver dispatch.

data.text: Design a ride-sharing platform like Uber. Riders request rides from their current location, the system finds the nearest available drivers within seconds, matches rider to driver, tracks both parties in real-time on a map, calculates dynamic pricing based on supply and demand, and handles the full lifecycle from request through trip completion and payment. The system must operate globally with 25 million trips per day, handling hundreds of thousands of concurrent active trips with sub-1s match times.

terms.definition: Hierarchical geocoding system that encodes lat/lon into a short string; nearby locations share prefix, enabling efficient proximity search.
Uber's geospatial indexing system using hexagonal cells at multiple resolutions, superior to square grids for uniform area coverage.
Dynamic pricing algorithm that increases fares when demand exceeds supply in a geographic area (> 1.0x multiplier).
Routing engine calculation accounting for real-time traffic, road network, and historical speed data.
Matching algorithm that assigns the optimal driver to each rider request, balancing proximity, ETA, and driver preferences.

data.title: Functional Requirements
items: Rider requests a ride from pickup location; system shows nearby drivers and ETA
Match rider to nearest available driver within 1 second
Real-time GPS location updates from driver app every 4-5 seconds
Rider and driver track each other on a live map during trip
Dynamic surge pricing based on supply/demand ratio per hexagonal cell
Trip lifecycle management: requested → accepted → en-route → arrived → in-progress → completed
Payment processing on trip completion (card, wallet, cash)
Driver earnings calculation with deductions and tip support
Ratings (1-5 stars) for both rider and driver after each trip

data.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items: 25 million trips/day (~290 trips/s average, ~5,000 trips/s peak)
1 million active drivers sending GPS every 5s = 200,000 location updates/second
Match time: <1 second from ride request to driver assignment
Location data freshness: driver position shown to rider within 5 seconds of update
99.99% availability for ride request and matching path
Geographic scaling: operations in 900+ cities across 70 countries
Location history retention: 30 days per trip for audit and dispute resolution

items.question: Why use H3 hexagonal grid instead of geohash?
items.answer: Hexagons have equal distance from center to all 6 neighbors (squares have different distances to corner vs edge neighbors). This makes H3 cells ideal for uniform coverage in supply/demand analysis and search radius expansion. Geohash has edge effects where nearby points span different prefixes at cell boundaries.

items.question: How does the matching algorithm work at scale?
items.answer: On ride request: (1) Query Redis GEO for all drivers within initial radius (~1km). (2) Rank by ETA using the routing engine. (3) Sequentially offer the trip to the top driver. (4) If declined or no response in 10s, try the next. The entire process must complete within 1 second, so ETA computation is parallelised for top candidates.

items.question: How do you handle 200K driver GPS updates per second?
items.answer: GPS events go to Kafka (message queue) for durability, then an async consumer updates Redis GEO index. Redis GEO uses a geohash-encoded sorted set internally, giving O(log N) position updates. Cassandra stores historical location trails partitioned by driver_id + date for trip replay and audit.

items.question: How does surge pricing work in practice?
items.answer: Every 30 seconds, the Demand Monitor counts ride requests per H3 cell; the Supply Monitor counts available drivers per cell. Surge = (demand rate) / (supply rate). If surge > 1.2, a multiplier is applied to the base fare and shown to riders with a warning. Surge cache TTL is 30s to reflect rapid supply/demand changes.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: H3 hexagonal grid enables uniform geospatial indexing for driver search and surge pricing
Redis GEO index holds all driver positions with 5s TTL — 200K updates/s is achievable with Redis Cluster
Matching pipeline: geo-search → ETA ranking → sequential driver offer → fallback expansion
Trip state machine ensures consistent lifecycle: each state transition is atomic and idempotent
Surge pricing uses rolling supply/demand ratios per cell, refreshed every 30 seconds
data.takeaway: Uber's key innovation is the real-time geospatial matching engine — efficiently finding the nearest available driver and computing accurate ETAs at scale while simultaneously managing dynamic pricing, trip state, and payment.
